pending.note: Bearing vibration. The catalogue defines no unit and the tag name cannot settle it: ISO 20816 covers both casing velocity in mm/s RMS, measured by an accelerometer, and relative shaft displacement in micrometres peak-to-peak, measured by a proximity probe. The trailing '2' hints at a second channel per bearing, which is the usual X/Y proximity-probe arrangement and would favour micrometres, but that is an inference about which instrument is fitted, not a fact about the tag. Picking the wrong one puts the reading out by orders of magnitude and would make every alarm threshold meaningless. Needs the instrument type per bearing. Recommended: Ask the site which is installed. If proximity probes, use 'um'; if accelerometers on the bearing housing, use 'mm/s'. Both validate in this system.

pending.note: Bearing vibration. The catalogue defines no unit and the tag name cannot settle it: ISO 20816 covers both casing velocity in mm/s RMS, measured by an accelerometer, and relative shaft displacement in micrometres peak-to-peak, measured by a proximity probe. The trailing '2' hints at a second channel per bearing, which is the usual X/Y proximity-probe arrangement and would favour micrometres, but that is an inference about which instrument is fitted, not a fact about the tag. Picking the wrong one puts the reading out by orders of magnitude and would make every alarm threshold meaningless. Needs the instrument type per bearing. Recommended: Ask the site which is installed. If proximity probes, use 'um'; if accelerometers on the bearing housing, use 'mm/s'. Both validate in this system.
